minuscule

/MIN-uh-skyool/ — rhymes with pool · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is minuscule is extremely small.

The artist painted an entire city scene on a minuscule grain of rice.

Worked Example

The paleontologist discovered minuscule fossils of ancient organisms no larger than a grain of sand, requiring a microscope to study them.

Minuscule captures the extreme smallness — not just small, but so tiny it is almost impossible to see or handle without magnification. This is much more extreme than 'small' and deserves its own precise word.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

diminutive: Diminutive means noticeably small in a neat, charming way — a diminutive cottage sounds inviting. It carries affection and says nothing about being hard to see. Minuscule is pure extremity: smallness so severe the eye can barely find the thing at all.

miniature: Miniature means built as a scaled-down copy of something larger — a miniature train has every part of the real one, just shrunk. Minuscule says nothing about being a model; it simply means extremely small, whatever the thing is and however it got that way.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

massive: huge in size, bulk, or weight

enormous: extremely large, far beyond normal size

Where it sits · how hard it is to see — small → tiny → microscopic → minuscule

small vs. minuscule: Small is far weaker than minuscule: small means below average in size, while minuscule means so extremely tiny it is hard even to notice.

tiny vs. minuscule: Tiny is strong but still weaker than minuscule — tiny things are very small yet easy to see, while minuscule things make you squint to find them.

microscopic vs. minuscule: Microscopic outdoes even minuscule: a minuscule speck can still be spotted with sharp eyes, but a microscopic one cannot be seen without a microscope.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — minus

Root — minus: less, smaller (Latin)

Suffix — -cule (Latin -culus)

Suffix — -cule (Latin -culus): little; a small version of something (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: In Latin, minusculus meant 'rather small' — minus ('less') plus the diminutive ending -culus ('little'). Stack 'less' and 'little' together and you get minuscule: extremely small.

Use the root in a new word: minimum

Use the root in a new word: minimum: The minimum is the smallest amount allowed — built on the same Latin root minus, 'less,' that makes minuscule mean extremely small.

Word Choice

formal

Minuscule is the precise word for something so extremely small it is almost invisible — use it for sizes that would require magnification or great effort to perceive. For things that are just small or tiny, use 'small' or 'tiny.'
